framework.name: CMMC Level 2
framework.description: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) 2.0 Level 2 (Advanced): the 110 security requirements of NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 for systems that process, store or transmit Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), in 14 families. Codes follow the CMMC Level 2 Assessment Guide v2 (DoD CIO); NIST SP 800-171 requirement text is a US government work and is quoted. Level 2 is assessed separately from Level 1 even where a practice is the same, because it protects CUI rather than Federal Contract Information.

supplementaryControls.title: Control of CUI on publicly accessible systems
supplementaryControls.description: Name who may post or process information on publicly accessible systems, have procedures that keep Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) from being posted or processed on them, review content before it is posted, review the content already on them for CUI, and have a way to remove and address an improper posting
supplementaryControls.question: For this publicly accessible system: is it defined who may post or process information on it, are there procedures that keep Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) from being posted or processed on it, is content reviewed before it is posted and reviewed again once published, and is there a way to remove and address an improper posting?
supplementaryControls.intent: CUI is not cleared for public release, and a post to a website, forum or social channel is hard to recall. Access control and data leakage prevention do not by themselves check what a permitted person publishes.
examples: Written list of the people allowed to publish to the website and social media accounts
Second-person review or approval step before content goes live, checking for CUI
Periodic review of public pages for CUI and other non-public information
Procedure to take down an improper posting and alert the people who need to know, including the contracting officer where the contract requires it
Guidance to staff that CUI, and contract documents that carry CUI markings, are not posted publicly

supplementaryControls.title: System use notification for CUI
supplementaryControls.description: Identify the privacy and security notices that the applicable Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) rules require, make them consistent and tied to the specific CUI category, and display them to users, for example as a warning banner before log-on or as a posted notice where a banner is not possible. Notices are needed only where people log on; a system with no human logon interface needs none
supplementaryControls.question: For this system that processes, stores or transmits Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI): if people log on to it, are the privacy and security notices required by the applicable CUI rules identified, consistent and associated with the CUI category, and are they displayed to users? A system with no human logon interface meets this without a notice.
supplementaryControls.intent: Users of a system that holds CUI need to be told, before they use it, that it is monitored, that use is limited to authorized purposes and that CUI rules apply. A general log-on banner does not by itself carry the notices the CUI rules specify, or show that legal counsel approved their wording.
examples: Log-on banner on each system with human log-on interfaces, with wording taken from the applicable CUI rules and approved by legal counsel
Register of the notices required for each CUI category in the contract, with the system and place where each is shown
Posters or printed notices where an automated banner is not possible
Periodic check, and after a contract or CUI category change, that the displayed notices still match the required wording

supplementaryControls.title: FIPS-validated cryptography for CUI
supplementaryControls.description: Use cryptography that has been validated under the Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) wherever cryptography protects the confidentiality of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), and keep a list of the validated modules and their validation certificates
supplementaryControls.question: For this system: wherever cryptography protects the confidentiality of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), in transit or at rest, is it FIPS-validated and is the validated module and its certificate recorded?
supplementaryControls.intent: Strong algorithms are not enough for CUI: the cryptographic module has to have been validated under FIPS. A product that merely implements an approved algorithm, or whose validation was revoked or does not cover the configuration in use, does not meet the practice. A module whose certificate has moved to the CMVP Historical list is not revoked; keeping it in an existing system needs a documented risk decision.
examples: List of the cryptographic modules protecting CUI, with their FIPS validation certificate numbers and status
Operating systems, VPNs and storage encryption run in their FIPS-validated mode, with the configuration setting recorded
Check of the validation status when a module is bought, updated or reaches the end of its validation
Procurement requirement that products protecting CUI use FIPS-validated modules

supplementaryControls.title: Collaborative computing devices: no remote activation, use indicated
supplementaryControls.description: Identify the collaborative computing devices (networked whiteboards, cameras, microphones) in places where Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) is discussed or shown, prohibit their remote activation, and make sure each shows the people present when it is in use
supplementaryControls.question: For the collaborative computing devices connected to this system: are they identified, is remote activation prohibited, and does each device indicate to users present that it is in use? Dedicated video conferencing systems that are activated only by a participant calling or connecting are excluded.
supplementaryControls.intent: A conference-room camera, microphone or whiteboard that can be switched on from elsewhere can capture CUI without anyone present knowing. Dedicated video conferencing systems that are activated only by a participant calling or connecting are outside the practice.
examples: Inventory of cameras, microphones, smart speakers and networked whiteboards, with their location
Remote-activation and auto-answer features disabled in device or management-console configuration
Indicator lights or on-screen signals shown when a camera or microphone is active, tested periodically
Physical shutters or disconnected microphones for devices in rooms where CUI is discussed and the indicator cannot be relied on

supplementaryControls.title: Insider threat awareness training
supplementaryControls.description: Identify the potential indicators of insider threat and train managers and employees to recognize them and to report them through the organization's channels, tailoring the content to role, to protect Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI)
supplementaryControls.intent: People with access to CUI are the most likely place a misuse of it starts or is first noticed. General security awareness training does not by itself teach what insider threat indicators look like or how to raise a concern about a colleague.
examples: Documented list of insider threat indicators, such as attempts to reach information not needed for the job and serious policy violations
Training module for employees and a separate one for managers on changes in the behaviour of team members
Reporting channel and procedure for concerns about a possible insider, with feedback that reports are handled
Training records showing managers and employees completed it, repeated on a set interval and for new joiners

supplementaryControls.title: System security plan for systems handling CUI
supplementaryControls.description: Develop and document a system security plan for each system that handles Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), describing its boundary, its environment of operation, how each security requirement is implemented, which requirements the designated authority has approved as not applicable, and its relationships with and connections to other systems, and update it at a defined frequency
supplementaryControls.question: For this system that handles Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI): is there a system security plan that describes the boundary, environment of operation, how each requirement is implemented, requirements approved as not applicable by the designated authority, and connections to other systems, and is it updated at a defined frequency?
supplementaryControls.intent: The plan is the document an assessor reads first and the record of what the CUI system is. The ISMS scope and the Statement of Applicability describe parts of it, but neither defines a system boundary, its environment and its connections, or states an update frequency.
examples: System security plan per CUI system, with boundary diagram and asset inventory
Description of the environment: hosting, locations, enclaves, external service providers and the CUI they handle
Implementation statement for each security requirement, and a record of those approved as not applicable and by whom
Table of connections to other systems with the interface and data exchanged
Stated update frequency (at least yearly, and after significant change) with review and approval records

requirements.title: Authorized Access Control
requirements.text: Limit system access to authorized users, processes acting on behalf of authorized users, and devices (including other systems). (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.1.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 AC.L1-b.1.i. Sets the access control rules, but does not by itself require identifying authorized processes and devices or limiting access to them.
Keeps the list of identities (users and systems) accurate, which is what authorized access is checked against; it does not enforce the limit.
Provisioning and removal of access rights for users; says nothing specific about processes or devices.
Network controls limit which devices and other systems can connect, covering the device part of the requirement only.

requirements.title: Transaction & Function Control
requirements.text: Limit system access to the types of transactions and functions that authorized users are permitted to execute. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.2.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 AC.L1-b.1.ii. Restricts access to information and functions according to the access control policy, which is this requirement.
Limits privileged functions only; ordinary user functions are covered by A.8.3.
Assigns the access rights that define which functions a user may execute; does not itself enforce them in the system.

requirements.title: Control CUI Flow
requirements.text: Control the flow of CUI in accordance with approved authorizations. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.3.)

mappings.rationale: Rules and agreements for transferring information control flow between parties, but not every internal flow of CUI, nor an approval per flow.
Segregating networks limits where CUI can flow between network zones; it does not cover flow control inside a zone or at the application level.
Network security controls such as firewalls and filters enforce permitted flows, without requiring them to be tied to approved authorizations for CUI.
Data leakage prevention detects and blocks CUI leaving through channels, but is not a general flow-control mechanism.

requirements.title: Separation of Duties
requirements.text: Separate the duties of individuals to reduce the risk of malevolent activity without collusion. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.4.)

mappings.rationale: Separating conflicting duties and areas of responsibility to reduce the risk of misuse is this requirement.

requirements.title: Least Privilege
requirements.text: Employ the principle of least privilege, including for specific security functions and privileged accounts. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.5.)

mappings.rationale: Need-to-know and need-to-use rules for access; does not by itself address security functions and privileged accounts specifically.
Restricts and manages privileged access rights, which covers privileged accounts and security functions but not least privilege for ordinary accounts.
Restricts access to information and functions per the access control policy; does not mandate the least-privilege principle as such.
Access rights are provisioned and reviewed against the access control policy, which supports least privilege without requiring it.

requirements.title: Non-Privileged Account Use
requirements.text: Use non-privileged accounts or roles when accessing nonsecurity functions. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.6.)

mappings.rationale: Privileged identities are used only for administrative tasks, with ordinary accounts used for everyday nonsecurity work, which is this requirement.

requirements.title: Privileged Functions
requirements.text: Prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions and capture the execution of such functions in audit logs. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.7.)

mappings.rationale: Restricts who holds privileged access rights, which keeps non-privileged users from privileged functions; does not require the execution of those functions to be logged.
Access restriction to functions per the access control policy; does not mention capturing privileged function execution.
Logging of privileged activity gives the audit record; does not by itself prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions.

requirements.title: Unsuccessful Logon Attempts
requirements.text: Limit unsuccessful logon attempts. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.8.)

mappings.rationale: Secure log-on procedures limit failed attempts and protect against brute-force attacks, which is this requirement.

requirements.title: Privacy & Security Notices
requirements.text: Provide privacy and security notices consistent with applicable CUI rules. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.9.)

mappings.rationale: Covers both assessment objectives: [a] the notices required by the CUI rules are identified, consistent and associated with the CUI category; [b] the notices are displayed.
Log-on procedures can show a general notice that access is for authorized users only; does not cover privacy notices or the applicable CUI rules.
Identifying the legal, statutory and regulatory requirements that apply (here CUI rules) informs the notice wording, but does not require notices to be provided.
Rules for acceptable use communicated to users overlap with the security notice; not a system use notification at access.

requirements.title: Session Lock
requirements.text: Use session lock with pattern-hiding displays to prevent access and viewing of data after a period of inactivity. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.10.)

mappings.rationale: Clear screen rules cover locking unattended screens; they do not require an automatic lock after inactivity with a pattern-hiding display.
Secure log-on includes session time-out after inactivity; does not require the pattern-hiding display.
Endpoint device rules usually cover automatic locking, but the Control is broader and does not guarantee it.

requirements.title: Session Termination
requirements.text: Terminate (automatically) a user session after a defined condition. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.11.)

mappings.rationale: Inactive sessions are shut down after a defined period, covering the most common condition; the requirement allows other defined conditions.
Endpoint device rules can include session time-outs; the Control is broader and does not guarantee automatic termination.

requirements.title: Control Remote Access
requirements.text: Monitor and control remote access sessions. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.12.)

mappings.rationale: Security measures for remote working cover remote access to systems; they do not require sessions to be monitored.
Network security covers controlling remote connections; does not require monitoring of each session.
Monitoring of networks and systems supplies the monitoring part; remote access sessions are not singled out.

requirements.title: Remote Access Confidentiality
requirements.text: Employ cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality of remote access sessions. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.13.)

mappings.rationale: Rules for the effective use of cryptography cover encrypting remote connections but do not require it for every remote access session.
Remote working security measures include secure remote access; encryption of the session is not specified.
Network security covers securing remote connections; does not require cryptographic mechanisms.

requirements.title: Remote Access Routing
requirements.text: Route remote access via managed access control points. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.14.)

mappings.rationale: Network controls can force remote access through VPN gateways or similar, but the Control does not require routing through managed access control points.
Segregation of networks supports a managed entry point for remote users; does not require it.
Remote working security measures cover how people connect from outside; routing through managed points is not specified.

requirements.title: Privileged Remote Access
requirements.text: Authorize remote execution of privileged commands and remote access to security-relevant information. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.15.)

mappings.rationale: Authorization of privileged access rights applies to remote privileged commands too; remote access to security-relevant information is not singled out.
Remote working measures cover who may work remotely and how; no separate authorization of privileged remote commands.
Access rights are authorized before they are granted, which includes remote privileged access; not specific to remote execution.

requirements.title: Wireless Access Authorization
requirements.text: Authorize wireless access prior to allowing such connections. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.16.)

mappings.rationale: Network security covers authorizing devices and connections to networks; wireless access is not singled out.
Security requirements for network services cover wireless as a service; does not require authorization before each connection.

requirements.title: Wireless Access Protection
requirements.text: Protect wireless access using authentication and encryption. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.17.)

mappings.rationale: Network security covers securing wireless networks; authentication and encryption are not both required.
Security mechanisms for network services include wireless; not specific to authentication and encryption.
Cryptography rules cover encrypting wireless traffic; the Control is broader and does not require wireless encryption.

requirements.title: Mobile Device Connection
requirements.text: Control connection of mobile devices. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.18.)

mappings.rationale: Rules for user endpoint devices, including mobile devices, cover how they are registered and connected; the Control is broader and does not guarantee connection control.
Network security controls which devices can connect, covering the connection part only.

requirements.title: Encrypt CUI on Mobile
requirements.text: Encrypt CUI on mobile devices and mobile computing platforms. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.19.)

mappings.rationale: Endpoint device rules usually require encryption of stored information on mobile devices; the Control is broader and does not guarantee it for CUI.
Cryptography rules cover encrypting stored information; they do not single out mobile devices and platforms.

requirements.title: External Connections
requirements.text: Verify and control/limit connections to and use of external systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.20.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 AC.L1-b.1.iii. Controls connections from the network side; it does not cover verifying and limiting use of external systems such as personal devices or third-party services.
Security requirements for network services used, which includes connections to external providers; not use of external systems by staff.
Covers connecting from outside the organization's premises; not every external system connection.
Covers control of cloud services as external systems; other external systems are not addressed.

requirements.title: Portable Storage Use
requirements.text: Limit use of portable storage devices on external systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.21.)

mappings.rationale: Storage media rules cover use of portable storage; they do not address using it on systems the organization does not control.
Acceptable use rules can limit use of portable storage on external systems, without requiring it.
Remote working measures cover working on systems outside the organization; portable storage is not singled out.

requirements.title: Control Public Information
requirements.text: Control CUI posted or processed on publicly accessible systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.1.22.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 AC.L1-b.1.iv. Covers all five assessment objectives [a]-[e]: who may post or process, procedures keeping CUI off public systems, review before posting, review of published content, and removal of an improper posting.
Helps prevent CUI leaking to public destinations but does not define who may post or require review before publication.
Rules for transferring information to other parties; not specific to posting on public systems.

requirements.title: Role-Based Risk Awareness
requirements.text: Ensure that managers, systems administrators, and users of organizational systems are made aware of the security risks associated with their activities and of the applicable policies, standards, and procedures related to the security of those systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.2.1.)

mappings.rationale: Awareness of the organization's policies and of the risks of one's own activities, tailored to job function, is this requirement.
Awareness of the policy and of one's contribution to the ISMS; narrower than the risks of each role's activities.

requirements.title: Role-Based Training
requirements.text: Ensure that personnel are trained to carry out their assigned information security-related duties and responsibilities. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.2.2.)

mappings.rationale: Appropriate training for the information security duties of a job function is this requirement.
Competence of people affecting security performance; covers training as one way to get there.

requirements.title: Insider Threat Awareness
requirements.text: Provide security awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.2.3.)

mappings.rationale: Covers both assessment objectives: [a] the potential indicators of insider threat are identified; [b] training on recognizing and reporting them is provided to managers and employees.
Awareness training can cover insider threat indicators, but the Control does not require the topic.
Reporting of observed security events covers reporting a suspected insider, without the recognition training.

requirements.title: System Auditing
requirements.text: Create and retain system audit logs and records to the extent needed to enable the monitoring, analysis, investigation, and reporting of unlawful or unauthorized system activity. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.3.1.)

mappings.rationale: Producing, storing, protecting and analysing logs of activities, exceptions and events is this requirement.

requirements.title: User Accountability
requirements.text: Ensure that the actions of individual system users can be uniquely traced to those users so they can be held accountable for their actions. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.3.2.)

mappings.rationale: Logs record user IDs and the activities performed, so actions can be traced to individual users.
Unique identities per person are what make a log entry traceable; the Control does not itself create the log.

requirements.title: Event Review
requirements.text: Review and update logged events. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.3.3.)

mappings.rationale: Logs are analysed, but the Control does not require reviewing and updating the set of logged events.
Monitoring includes reviewing records for anomalies; it does not cover updating what is logged.

requirements.title: Audit Failure Alerting
requirements.text: Alert in the event of an audit logging process failure. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.3.4.)

mappings.rationale: Logging facilities are protected, but alerting when the logging process fails is not required.
Monitoring of systems can include the health of logging, without requiring an alert on logging failure.

requirements.title: Audit Correlation
requirements.text: Correlate audit record review, analysis, and reporting processes for investigation and response to indications of unlawful, unauthorized, suspicious, or unusual activity. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.3.5.)

mappings.rationale: Log analysis may correlate events, but the Control does not require correlating review, analysis and reporting for response.
Monitoring for anomalous behaviour supports correlation; the Control does not require a correlation process.

requirements.title: Reduction & Reporting
requirements.text: Provide audit record reduction and report generation to support on-demand analysis and reporting. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.3.6.)

mappings.rationale: Logs are analysed and reported on, but audit record reduction and on-demand reporting are not required.

requirements.title: Authoritative Time Source
requirements.text: Provide a system capability that compares and synchronizes internal system clocks with an authoritative source to generate time stamps for audit records. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.3.7.)

mappings.rationale: Synchronising the clocks of information processing systems to approved time sources is this requirement.

requirements.title: Audit Protection
requirements.text: Protect audit information and audit logging tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.3.8.)

mappings.rationale: Protecting logging facilities and log information against tampering and unauthorized access is part of this Control and is this requirement.

requirements.title: Audit Management
requirements.text: Limit management of audit logging functionality to a subset of privileged users. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.3.9.)

mappings.rationale: Protects logging facilities from unauthorized change, without limiting management of logging to a subset of privileged users.
Restricts privileged access rights, which keeps audit management among a few privileged users; logging is not singled out.

requirements.title: System Baselining
requirements.text: Establish and maintain baseline configurations and inventories of organizational systems (including hardware, software, firmware, and documentation) throughout the respective system development life cycles. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.4.1.)

mappings.rationale: Configurations, including security configurations, are established and documented; inventories and the full system life cycle are not covered.
Inventory of information and other assets covers the inventory part; baseline configurations are not covered.

requirements.title: Security Configuration Enforcement
requirements.text: Establish and enforce security configuration settings for information technology products employed in organizational systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.4.2.)

mappings.rationale: Establishing, implementing, monitoring and reviewing security configurations of hardware, software and services is this requirement.

requirements.title: System Change Management
requirements.text: Track, review, approve or disapprove, and log changes to organizational systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.4.3.)

mappings.rationale: Changes to information processing facilities and systems under change management procedures, with review, approval and logging, is this requirement.

requirements.title: Security Impact Analysis
requirements.text: Analyze the security impact of changes prior to implementation. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.4.4.)

mappings.rationale: Change management includes assessing the impact of a change; the Control does not require the analysis to cover security specifically.
Security testing before acceptance helps show the impact of a change; it is aimed at development and acceptance.

requirements.title: Access Restrictions for Change
requirements.text: Define, document, approve, and enforce physical and logical access restrictions associated with changes to organizational systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.4.5.)

mappings.rationale: Change management covers who may make and approve changes; physical and logical access restrictions are not explicit.
Restricts privileged access, which is what logical change access depends on.
Separating development, test and production environments limits who can change production; not all changes are in that scope.

requirements.title: Least Functionality
requirements.text: Employ the principle of least functionality by configuring organizational systems to provide only essential capabilities. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.4.6.)

mappings.rationale: Secure configurations normally remove unneeded capabilities, but the Control does not require least functionality.
Controls installation of software on operational systems, which limits capabilities; not configuration of the system as a whole.

requirements.title: Nonessential Functionality
requirements.text: Restrict, disable, or prevent the use of nonessential programs, functions, ports, protocols, and services. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.4.7.)

mappings.rationale: Secure configuration can disable unneeded functions; the Control does not name programs, ports, protocols and services.
Network security covers limiting ports, protocols and services; programs and functions are not covered.

requirements.title: Application Execution Policy
requirements.text: Apply deny-by-exception (blacklisting) policy to prevent the use of unauthorized software or deny-all, permit-by-exception (whitelisting) policy to allow the execution of authorized software. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.4.8.)

mappings.rationale: Rules for installing software on operational systems; allow-listing or deny-listing of execution is not required.
Malware protection guidance mentions application allow-listing as one measure; it is not required.

requirements.title: User-Installed Software
requirements.text: Control and monitor user-installed software. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.4.9.)

mappings.rationale: Rules governing installation of software by users are established and implemented; monitoring user-installed software is not required.
Monitoring of systems can detect unauthorized installations, without requiring it.

requirements.title: Identification
requirements.text: Identify system users, processes acting on behalf of users, and devices. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.5.1.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 IA.L1-b.1.v. Managing the full life cycle of identities, for people and systems, gives each user, process and device a unique identity.

requirements.title: Authentication
requirements.text: Authenticate (or verify) the identities of users, processes, or devices, as a prerequisite to allowing access to organizational systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.5.2.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 IA.L1-b.1.vi. Secure authentication for all access is the control that verifies identity before access is granted.
Management of authentication credentials such as passwords and keys; supports but is not the verification itself.

requirements.title: Multifactor Authentication
requirements.text: Use multifactor authentication for local and network access to privileged accounts and for network access to non-privileged accounts. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.5.3.)

mappings.rationale: Secure authentication includes multi-factor methods where the risk calls for them; the Control does not require MFA for privileged and network access.
Privileged access rights are tied to authentication strength by the access control policy; MFA is not stated.

requirements.title: Replay-Resistant Authentication
requirements.text: Employ replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for network access to privileged and non-privileged accounts. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.5.4.)

mappings.rationale: Secure authentication covers protecting authentication from being captured and reused; replay resistance is not named.
Cryptographic mechanisms are a typical way to resist replay, but the Control does not require it for authentication.

requirements.title: Identifier Reuse
requirements.text: Prevent reuse of identifiers for a defined period. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.5.5.)

mappings.rationale: Managing identities across their life cycle, including not reassigning an identity to another person, is this requirement.

requirements.title: Identifier Handling
requirements.text: Disable identifiers after a defined period of inactivity. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.5.6.)

mappings.rationale: Identities are disabled or removed when no longer needed and redundant identities are reviewed; a defined period of inactivity is not required.
Access rights are reviewed and removed when no longer needed, which supports disabling inactive accounts.

requirements.title: Password Complexity
requirements.text: Enforce a minimum password complexity and change of characters when new passwords are created. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.5.7.)

mappings.rationale: Rules for passwords and other authentication information include strength; a minimum complexity and a change of characters are not specified.
Secure authentication covers password quality at a high level only.

requirements.title: Password Reuse
requirements.text: Prohibit password reuse for a specified number of generations. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.5.8.)

mappings.rationale: Allocation and management of authentication information covers password changes; prohibiting reuse for a number of generations is not required.

requirements.title: Temporary Passwords
requirements.text: Allow temporary password use for system logons with an immediate change to a permanent password. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.5.9.)

mappings.rationale: Initial and temporary authentication information is issued securely and must be changed at first use, which is this requirement.

requirements.title: Cryptographically-Protected Passwords
requirements.text: Store and transmit only cryptographically-protected passwords. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.5.10.)

mappings.rationale: Authentication information is kept confidential and stored and transmitted securely; cryptographic protection is not mandated.
Cryptography rules cover protecting stored and transmitted credentials without requiring it.

requirements.title: Obscure Feedback
requirements.text: Obscure feedback of authentication information. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.5.11.)

mappings.rationale: Secure log-on does not display the password or other authentication information while it is entered, which is this requirement.

requirements.title: Incident Handling
requirements.text: Establish an operational incident-handling capability for organizational systems that includes preparation, detection, analysis, containment, recovery, and user response activities. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.6.1.)

mappings.rationale: Planning and preparing incident management, with defined processes and roles across the incident life cycle, is this requirement.
Assessing and deciding on events covers detection and analysis; not preparation, recovery or user response.
Responding to incidents covers containment and recovery; not preparation or detection.
Monitoring supplies detection; the rest of the incident-handling capability is out of scope.

requirements.title: Incident Reporting
requirements.text: Track, document, and report incidents to designated officials and/or authorities both internal and external to the organization. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.6.2.)

mappings.rationale: Mechanism for reporting events and weaknesses; reporting to external authorities is not covered.
Contact with relevant authorities covers external reporting; internal tracking and documentation are not covered.
Response includes recording and escalating incidents; reporting to external bodies is not specified.

requirements.title: Incident Response Testing
requirements.text: Test the organizational incident response capability. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.6.3.)

mappings.rationale: Incident management planning may include exercises, but testing is not strictly required.
Learning from incidents improves the capability; it is not a test of it.

requirements.title: Perform Maintenance
requirements.text: Perform maintenance on organizational systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.7.1.)

mappings.rationale: Maintaining equipment correctly so availability, integrity and confidentiality are preserved is this requirement.

requirements.title: System Maintenance Control
requirements.text: Provide controls on the tools, techniques, mechanisms, and personnel used to conduct system maintenance. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.7.2.)

mappings.rationale: Equipment maintenance covers the personnel and processes used; controls on tools and techniques are not explicit.
Restricts privileged access, which governs use of maintenance tools and accounts.

requirements.title: Equipment Sanitization
requirements.text: Ensure equipment removed for off-site maintenance is sanitized of any CUI. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.7.3.)

mappings.rationale: Sanitising equipment before disposal or re-use; off-site maintenance is not a disposal.
Equipment maintenance covers handling of equipment sent off-site, with sanitisation only as a possible measure.
Protecting assets off-premises covers equipment sent away; sanitisation is not required.

requirements.title: Media Inspection
requirements.text: Check media containing diagnostic and test programs for malicious code before the media are used in organizational systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.7.4.)

mappings.rationale: Malware controls cover scanning media before use; diagnostic and test program media are not singled out.
Equipment maintenance covers maintenance activity; checking the media brought by maintenance staff is not required.

requirements.title: Nonlocal Maintenance
requirements.text: Require multifactor authentication to establish nonlocal maintenance sessions via external network connections and terminate such connections when nonlocal maintenance is complete. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.7.5.)

mappings.rationale: Secure authentication includes multi-factor methods; not required for maintenance sessions.
Equipment maintenance covers remote maintenance as an activity; session MFA and termination are not specified.

requirements.title: Maintenance Personnel
requirements.text: Supervise the maintenance activities of maintenance personnel without required access authorization. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.7.6.)

mappings.rationale: Equipment maintenance covers personnel doing the maintenance; supervision of personnel without access authorization is not specified.
Working in secure areas includes supervising third parties; not specific to maintenance.

requirements.title: Media Protection
requirements.text: Protect (i.e., physically control and securely store) system media containing CUI, both paper and digital. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.8.1.)

mappings.rationale: Managing storage media through their life cycle, with secure storage and handling of paper and digital media, is this requirement.

requirements.title: Media Access
requirements.text: Limit access to CUI on system media to authorized users. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.8.2.)

mappings.rationale: Storage media management includes who may use and handle media; the Control is broader.
Restricts access to information per the access control policy, including on media.
Access control rules cover who may reach CUI; media are not singled out.

requirements.title: Media Disposal
requirements.text: Sanitize or destroy system media containing CUI before disposal or release for reuse. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.8.3.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 MP.L1-b.1.vii. Sanitising or destroying equipment (including its storage media) before disposal or re-use is this requirement.
Covers the life cycle of storage media including disposal, but is broader and does not on its own guarantee sanitisation of media containing CUI, nor non-digital media such as paper.

requirements.title: Media Markings
requirements.text: Mark media with necessary CUI markings and distribution limitations. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.8.4.)

mappings.rationale: Information is labelled to the organization's classification scheme; CUI markings and distribution limitations are not specified.
Classification of information identifies what needs marking; it does not mark media.

requirements.title: Media Accountability
requirements.text: Control access to media containing CUI and maintain accountability for media during transport outside of controlled areas. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.8.5.)

mappings.rationale: Storage media in transit are protected and tracked; accountability for CUI media specifically is not required.
Information transfer rules cover physical media in transit; not accountability records.

requirements.title: Portable Storage Encryption
requirements.text: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality of CUI stored on digital media during transport unless otherwise protected by alternative physical safeguards. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.8.6.)

mappings.rationale: Cryptography rules cover protecting stored information; not specifically media in transport.
Storage media management includes protecting media in transit, with encryption as one option.

requirements.title: Removable Media
requirements.text: Control the use of removable media on system components. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.8.7.)

mappings.rationale: A policy for managing removable storage media, including authorization and controlling their use, is this requirement.

requirements.title: Shared Media
requirements.text: Prohibit the use of portable storage devices when such devices have no identifiable owner. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.8.8.)

mappings.rationale: Storage media management covers authorised media; a ban on media without an identifiable owner is not stated.
Assets have owners in the inventory, which makes an unowned device identifiable; no use prohibition.

requirements.title: Protect Backups
requirements.text: Protect the confidentiality of backup CUI at storage locations. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.8.9.)

mappings.rationale: Backup copies are kept and tested; confidentiality of backups at storage locations is not the focus of the Control.
Cryptography rules cover encrypting backups without requiring it.
Storage media management covers securing backup media; not backups held online.

requirements.title: Screen Individuals
requirements.text: Screen individuals prior to authorizing access to organizational systems containing CUI. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.9.1.)

mappings.rationale: Background verification of candidates before they join and before access is given is this requirement.

requirements.title: Personnel Actions
requirements.text: Ensure that organizational systems containing CUI are protected during and after personnel actions such as terminations and transfers. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.9.2.)

mappings.rationale: Access rights are modified or removed when employment ends or a role changes, which is what protects systems during and after personnel actions.
Return of assets on termination or transfer; does not cover removing access.
Responsibilities that remain after termination or change of employment; not the removal of access.

requirements.title: Limit Physical Access
requirements.text: Limit physical access to organizational systems, equipment, and the respective operating environments to authorized individuals. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.10.1.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 PE.L1-b.1.viii. Controls physical access to secure areas with appropriate authentication, limiting entry to authorized individuals.
Defines the perimeters of the areas that hold systems, which entry controls then protect.
Secures offices, rooms and facilities where the systems and equipment are located.

requirements.title: Monitor Facility
requirements.text: Protect and monitor the physical facility and support infrastructure for organizational systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.10.2.)

mappings.rationale: Monitoring premises with surveillance and alarms covers the monitoring part; protection of support infrastructure is not covered.
Defining physical security perimeters protects the facility; monitoring is not covered.
Securing offices, rooms and facilities protects the facility; monitoring is not covered.
Supporting utilities (power, cooling) protects part of the support infrastructure; the Control is narrower than the facility.

requirements.title: Escort Visitors
requirements.text: Escort visitors and monitor visitor activity. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.10.3.)

mappings.rationale: Narrower than CMMC Level 1 PE.L1-b.1.ix, which covers this practice together with 3.10.4 and 3.10.5. Physical entry controls normally cover visitor handling, but the Control does not on its own require escorting visitors.
Monitoring of premises supports watching visitor activity; it does not require visitors to be escorted.

requirements.title: Physical Access Logs
requirements.text: Maintain audit logs of physical access. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.10.4.)

mappings.rationale: Narrower than CMMC Level 1 PE.L1-b.1.ix, which covers this practice together with 3.10.3 and 3.10.5. Physical entry controls normally include entry logs, but the Control does not on its own require audit logs of physical access.
Monitoring of premises supports keeping records of physical access; it does not require audit logs.

requirements.title: Manage Physical Access
requirements.text: Control and manage physical access devices. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.10.5.)

mappings.rationale: Narrower than CMMC Level 1 PE.L1-b.1.ix, which covers this practice together with 3.10.3 and 3.10.4. Physical entry controls cover entry mechanisms, but the Control does not on its own require managing keys, badges and other physical access devices.
Return of assets covers recovering keys and badges when someone leaves; it does not cover inventory or day-to-day management of physical access devices.

requirements.title: Alternative Work Sites
requirements.text: Enforce safeguarding measures for CUI at alternate work sites. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.10.6.)

mappings.rationale: Security measures when personnel work remotely, to protect information accessed or processed outside the premises, are this requirement.
Protecting equipment and assets off-premises covers part of an alternate work site.

requirements.title: Risk Assessments
requirements.text: Periodically assess the risk to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, and individuals, resulting from the operation of organizational systems and the associated processing, storage, or transmission of CUI. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.11.1.)

mappings.rationale: Performing information security risk assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes occur is this requirement.
Defines the risk assessment process and criteria; the assessments themselves are done under clause 8.2.

requirements.title: Vulnerability Scan
requirements.text: Scan for vulnerabilities in organizational systems and applications periodically and when new vulnerabilities affecting those systems and applications are identified. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.11.2.)

mappings.rationale: Obtaining information on technical vulnerabilities, evaluating exposure and scanning for them, in a timely manner, is this requirement.
Threat intelligence supplies information on newly identified vulnerabilities and attacks; it does not scan systems.

requirements.title: Vulnerability Remediation
requirements.text: Remediate vulnerabilities in accordance with risk assessments. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.11.3.)

mappings.rationale: Taking appropriate measures, with timelines, to address vulnerabilities according to the risk is this requirement.
Risk treatment implemented per the plan; the Control is broader than vulnerabilities.

requirements.title: Security Control Assessment
requirements.text: Periodically assess the security controls in organizational systems to determine if the controls are effective in their application. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.12.1.)

mappings.rationale: Independent review of information security at planned intervals to confirm the continued suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of controls is this requirement.
Monitoring and measuring performance and ISMS effectiveness; the Control is broader than an assessment of each security control.
Compliance with policies, rules and standards is reviewed regularly; effectiveness is not the focus.

requirements.title: Operational Plan of Action
requirements.text: Develop and implement plans of action designed to correct deficiencies and reduce or eliminate vulnerabilities in organizational systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.12.2.)

mappings.rationale: Nonconformities are corrected with corrective action; vulnerabilities in systems are not singled out.
A risk treatment plan covers planned action to reduce risk; milestones for correcting deficiencies are not required.

requirements.title: Security Control Monitoring
requirements.text: Monitor security controls on an ongoing basis to ensure the continued effectiveness of the controls. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.12.3.)

mappings.rationale: Determining what to monitor and measure and evaluating ISMS performance and effectiveness on an ongoing basis is this requirement.
Regular review of compliance with policies and standards supports ongoing monitoring of controls.
Monitoring of networks and systems covers technical monitoring, not all security controls.

requirements.title: System Security Plan
requirements.text: Develop, document, and periodically update system security plans that describe system boundaries, system environments of operation, how security requirements are implemented, and the relationships with or connections to other systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.12.4.)

mappings.rationale: Covers all eight assessment objectives: [a] a plan is developed; [b] boundary, [c] environment of operation, [e] implementation method and [f] connections are described and documented in it; [d] requirements approved as not applicable are identified; [g] an update frequency is defined; [h] the plan is updated at that frequency.
Defines and documents the ISMS scope and boundaries; system environments and connections are not required.
The Statement of Applicability records how each Control is implemented; it is not a system security plan.
Documented information is created, updated and controlled; the plan's content is not specified.

requirements.title: Boundary Protection
requirements.text: Monitor, control, and protect communications (i.e., information transmitted or received by organizational systems) at the external boundaries and key internal boundaries of organizational systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.1.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 SC.L1-b.1.x. Network security (firewalls, restricted traffic) controls boundary traffic, but the Control does not on its own require monitoring of communications at the external and key internal boundaries.
Segregating networks creates the key internal boundaries; it does not itself monitor or control traffic across them.
Monitoring of network activity supplies the monitoring part; the boundary scope is not specified.

requirements.title: Security Engineering
requirements.text: Employ architectural designs, software development techniques, and systems engineering principles that promote effective information security within organizational systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.2.)

mappings.rationale: Principles for engineering secure systems, applied to any information system development, are this requirement.
Secure development life cycle covers development techniques; architecture and systems engineering are in A.8.27.

requirements.title: Role Separation
requirements.text: Separate user functionality from system management functionality. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.3.)

mappings.rationale: Segregation of duties separates conflicting functions; not the technical separation of user and management functionality.
Privileged access rights restrict management functions to administrators.
Segregation of networks can place management interfaces apart from user traffic.

requirements.title: Shared Resource Control
requirements.text: Prevent unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.4.)

mappings.rationale: Network segregation limits transfer between groups of systems; shared processors and storage are not addressed.
Secure engineering principles include isolation between workloads; not required.
Information deletion covers removing information from reused storage; not shared memory and processors.

requirements.title: Public-Access System Separation
requirements.text: Implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are physically or logically separated from internal networks. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.5.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 SC.L1-b.1.xi. Segregation of networks (for example a DMZ for public-facing components) is the usual way to meet this, but the Control does not require public-access components specifically to be separated.
Network security rules keep public-facing components from reaching internal networks, without requiring separate subnetworks.

requirements.title: Network Communication by Exception
requirements.text: Deny network communications traffic by default and allow network communications traffic by exception (i.e., deny all, permit by exception). (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.6.)

mappings.rationale: Network security rules restrict traffic; deny-by-default is not stated.
Segregated networks are usually closed by default, but this is not required.

requirements.title: Split Tunneling
requirements.text: Prevent remote devices from simultaneously establishing non-remote connections with organizational systems and communicating via some other connection to resources in external networks (i.e., split tunneling). (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.7.)

mappings.rationale: Network security covers controlling remote connections; split tunneling is not named.
Remote working measures can forbid split tunneling, without requiring it.

requirements.title: Data in Transit
requirements.text: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure of CUI during transmission unless otherwise protected by alternative physical safeguards. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.8.)

mappings.rationale: Cryptography rules cover encrypting information in transit; the Control does not require it for CUI.
Information transfer rules cover protecting information in transit; encryption is one option.

requirements.title: Connections Termination
requirements.text: Terminate network connections associated with communications sessions at the end of the sessions or after a defined period of inactivity. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.9.)

mappings.rationale: Secure log-on includes shutting down inactive sessions; network connections of non-user sessions are not covered.
Network security covers connection management; session end and inactivity timeouts are not required.

requirements.title: Key Management
requirements.text: Establish and manage cryptographic keys for cryptography employed in organizational systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.10.)

mappings.rationale: Rules for cryptography that include key management through the whole life cycle are this requirement.

requirements.title: CUI Encryption
requirements.text: Employ FIPS-validated cryptography when used to protect the confidentiality of CUI. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.11.)

mappings.rationale: Covers the single assessment objective [a]: FIPS-validated cryptography is employed to protect the confidentiality of CUI.
Cryptography rules require suitable algorithms and key lengths; FIPS-validated cryptography is not required.

requirements.title: Collaborative Device Control
requirements.text: Prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices and provide indication of devices in use to users present at the device. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.12.)

mappings.rationale: Covers all three assessment objectives: [a] collaborative computing devices are identified; [b] devices indicate to users when in use; [c] remote activation is prohibited.
Endpoint device rules can cover cameras and microphones; remote activation and in-use indication are not named.
Secure configuration can disable remote activation, without requiring it.

requirements.title: Mobile Code
requirements.text: Control and monitor the use of mobile code. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.13.)

mappings.rationale: Malware protection covers blocking malicious code, including malicious mobile code; control and monitoring of mobile code are not required.
Web filtering restricts access to sites that deliver mobile code; not all mobile code.

requirements.title: Voice over Internet Protocol
requirements.text: Control and monitor the use of Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) technologies. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.14.)

mappings.rationale: Network security covers voice traffic as network traffic; VoIP is not singled out.
Security of network services includes telephony providers; monitoring of VoIP use is not covered.

requirements.title: Communications Authenticity
requirements.text: Protect the authenticity of communications sessions. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.15.)

mappings.rationale: Cryptography rules cover authenticating communications; session authenticity is not required.
Network security controls protect communications; session authenticity is not specified.

requirements.title: Data at Rest
requirements.text: Protect the confidentiality of CUI at rest. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.13.16.)

mappings.rationale: Cryptography rules cover encrypting stored information; the Control does not require it for CUI at rest.
Restricts access to information, including stored information; confidentiality at rest otherwise depends on encryption.

requirements.title: Flaw Remediation
requirements.text: Identify, report, and correct system flaws in a timely manner. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.14.1.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 SI.L1-b.1.xii. Identifying, evaluating and remediating technical vulnerabilities, with timelines for fixing them, matches flaw remediation.

requirements.title: Malicious Code Protection
requirements.text: Provide protection from malicious code at designated locations within organizational systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.14.2.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 SI.L1-b.1.xiii. Malware detection, prevention and recovery controls on endpoints and servers are this requirement.

requirements.title: Security Alerts & Advisories
requirements.text: Monitor system security alerts and advisories and take action in response. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.14.3.)

mappings.rationale: Obtaining information on technical vulnerabilities and acting on it covers vulnerability advisories; security alerts in general are not covered.
Collecting and analysing threat information; taking action is not required.
Contact with special interest groups gives access to alerts and advisories; no requirement to act.

requirements.title: Update Malicious Code Protection
requirements.text: Update malicious code protection mechanisms when new releases are available. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.14.4.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 SI.L1-b.1.xiv. Requires malware protection to be in place and kept effective, but does not by itself guarantee that updates are applied as new releases appear.

requirements.title: System & File Scanning
requirements.text: Perform periodic scans of organizational systems and real-time scans of files from external sources as files are downloaded, opened, or executed. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.14.5.)

mappings.rationale: Same mapping as CMMC Level 1 SI.L1-b.1.xv. Scheduled scans are a typical part of malware protection, but the Control does not by itself require both periodic scans and real-time scans of files from external sources.

requirements.title: Monitor Communications for Attacks
requirements.text: Monitor organizational systems, including inbound and outbound communications traffic, to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.14.6.)

mappings.rationale: Monitoring networks, systems and applications for anomalous behaviour, including network traffic, is this requirement.
Network security controls traffic; detecting attacks is monitoring rather than control.

requirements.title: Identify Unauthorized Use
requirements.text: Identify unauthorized use of organizational systems. (NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 3.14.7.)

mappings.rationale: Monitoring for anomalous behaviour and unauthorized access or use of systems is this requirement.
Logs provide the record that unauthorized use is identified from; identification is not itself required.
